name: Panic disorder
aliases: Panic disorder with or without agoraphobia
summary: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks with persistent worry or avoidance. FDA-labeled options are fluoxetine, paroxetine (IR/CR), sertraline, venlafaxine XR, alprazolam (IR/ODT/XR), and clonazepam. Benzodiazepines carry boxed warnings for opioid co-use, misuse, and dependence/withdrawal.
plainSummary: Panic disorder causes sudden waves of intense fear with a racing heart, shortness of breath, or dizziness, plus worry about the next attack. Therapy (CBT) and daily medicines can help.

approved.indication: Acute treatment of Panic Disorder, with or without agoraphobia.

dosing.max: 60 mg/day (doses above 60 mg not systematically evaluated)
dosing.notes: Consider increase after several weeks if no improvement. Long half-life (norfluoxetine); lower or less frequent dosing in hepatic impairment and the elderly.

boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults
contraindications: MAOIs concurrently, within 5 weeks of stopping fluoxetine, or within 14 days of stopping an MAOI; starting in patients on linezolid or IV methylene blue
Thioridazine (and within 5 weeks of stopping fluoxetine)
approved.plainSummary: Fluoxetine is a daily antidepressant (SSRI) approved to treat panic disorder in adults. It is started at a low dose to avoid feeling jittery.

verified.note: Drugs@FDA lists Prozac capsule products as discontinued, though the Prozac label remains on DailyMed (Jan 2026); generic fluoxetine is widely available. Panic indication approved Jan 2003 (Drugs@FDA efficacy supplement).

approved.indication: Treatment of panic disorder (PD) in adults.

dosing.start: IR: 10 mg once daily; CR: 12.5 mg once daily
dosing.target: Titrate weekly (IR by 10 mg/day; CR by 12.5 mg/day) to response
dosing.notes: Geriatric, severe renal or hepatic impairment: IR start 10 mg, max 40 mg/day; CR start 12.5 mg, max 50 mg/day. Swallow CR tablets whole. Taper to stop.

boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults
contraindications: MAOIs (including linezolid or IV methylene blue) concurrently or within 14 days
Drugs that prolong the QTc interval and are CYP2D6 substrates (e.g., thioridazine, pimozide)
approved.plainSummary: Paroxetine is a daily antidepressant (SSRI) approved for panic disorder in adults. Stopping it suddenly can cause withdrawal-like symptoms.

verified.note: Paxil CR panic indication and dosing confirmed on the Paxil CR label (https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=483bd97f-c4d0-4e23-aaa8-6334f4471e0c). Approval year is for Paxil IR (1996).

dosing.start: 25 mg once daily for 1 week, then 50 mg
dosing.notes: Increase by 25–50 mg/day once weekly. Mild hepatic impairment: half the usual dose; not recommended in moderate or severe impairment. Oral concentrate must be diluted.

boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults
contraindications: MAOIs (including linezolid or IV methylene blue) concurrently or within 14 days
approved.plainSummary: Sertraline is a daily antidepressant (SSRI) approved for panic disorder in adults. It is started low and raised slowly.

approved.indication: Treatment of Panic Disorder (PD) in adults.

dosing.notes: Increase by up to 75 mg/day at intervals of at least 7 days. Hepatic impairment: reduce dose by 50% or more. Renal impairment: reduce 25–50% (50% or more in severe impairment/dialysis). Monitor blood pressure.

boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults
contraindications: MAOIs (including linezolid or IV methylene blue) concurrently or within 14 days
approved.plainSummary: Venlafaxine XR is a once-daily antidepressant (SNRI) approved for panic disorder in adults.

verified.note: Venlafaxine ER tablets and IR tablets are not labeled for panic disorder.

approved.indication: Treatment of panic disorder (PD), with or without agoraphobia, in adults (Xanax and Xanax XR).

dosing.start: IR/ODT: 0.5 mg three times daily; XR: 0.5–1 mg once daily (morning)
dosing.target: IR: individualized (trial mean about 5–6 mg/day); XR: 3–6 mg once daily
dosing.max: Up to 10 mg/day in occasional patients (trial range 1–10 mg/day)
dosing.notes: Increase by no more than 1 mg/day every 3–4 days. Reassess and consider dose reduction above 4 mg/day. Taper by no more than 0.5 mg every 3 days (often slower). Geriatric, hepatic impairment, and ritonavir require lower doses. Swallow XR whole.

boxedWarnings: Concomitant use with opioids may cause profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death
Abuse, misuse, and addiction, which can lead to overdose or death
Physical dependence and withdrawal reactions; abrupt discontinuation or rapid dose reduction can cause life-threatening withdrawal
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to alprazolam or other benzodiazepines
Strong CYP3A inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole), except ritonavir
approved.plainSummary: Alprazolam is a benzodiazepine approved for panic disorder in adults. It works quickly but can cause dependence, and stopping it must be done slowly.

verified.note: Xanax XR (https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=c8990714-c2f5-4b0c-9f1c-91d77156d962) and generic alprazolam ODT labels also checked. Approval year is for Xanax panic indication (1990); Xanax XR approved 2003.

approved.indication: Treatment of panic disorder, with or without agoraphobia (also labeled for seizure disorders).

dosing.notes: Higher fixed doses were less effective than 1 mg/day in trials. If needed, increase by 0.125–0.25 mg twice daily every 3 days. Taper by 0.125 mg twice daily every 3 days. No trial experience under 18 years.

boxedWarnings: Concomitant use with opioids may cause profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death
Abuse, misuse, and addiction, which can lead to overdose or death
Physical dependence and withdrawal reactions; abrupt discontinuation or rapid dose reduction can cause life-threatening withdrawal
contraindications: Clinical or biochemical evidence of significant liver disease
approved.plainSummary: Clonazepam is a longer-acting benzodiazepine approved for panic disorder in adults. It can cause sleepiness and dependence and should be stopped slowly.

offLabel.notes: SSRIs are first-line in APA and NICE guidance; escitalopram and citalopram are licensed for panic disorder in the UK but not FDA-labeled for it. Start low to limit early jitteriness. Citalopram has dose-related QT prolongation.

details.labeledFor: FDA-approved for depression and (escitalopram) GAD; neither is FDA-labeled for panic disorder.

dosing.start: Escitalopram 5 mg or citalopram 10 mg daily
dosing.target: Escitalopram 10–20 mg or citalopram 20–40 mg daily
dosing.max: Escitalopram 20 mg/day; citalopram 40 mg/day (20 mg over age 60)
dosing.notes: Start low to limit early jitteriness.

boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults
details.plainSummary: These SSRIs are first-line in guidelines for panic disorder, even though their labels do not list it.

references.label: NICE CG113: Generalised anxiety disorder and panic disorder in adults (recommendations)
APA Practice Guideline for Panic Disorder, 2nd ed. (2009; legacy guideline)
Bighelli et al. 2018, Cochrane: Antidepressants versus placebo for panic disorder in adults

offLabel.use: Panic disorder when SSRIs are unsuitable or ineffective
offLabel.notes: NICE: consider if an SSRI is unsuitable or there is no improvement after 12 weeks. Cautions: anticholinergic effects, orthostasis, cardiac conduction effects, lethality in overdose.

details.labeledFor: Imipramine and clomipramine are FDA-approved for depression (imipramine) and OCD (clomipramine); not for panic disorder.

dosing.target: Imipramine 100–200 mg/day (about 2.25 mg/kg in trials); clomipramine 50–150 mg/day
dosing.notes: Increase slowly because early anxiety is common.

boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults
contraindications: Acute recovery period after myocardial infarction
warnings: Anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, confusion)
Orthostasis and cardiac conduction effects; ECG in at-risk patients
Lowers the seizure threshold; may trigger mania
Highly toxic in overdose; limit quantities
details.plainSummary: Older antidepressants that can treat panic disorder when SSRIs do not work or are not tolerated. They are dangerous in overdose.

references.label: NICE CG113: Generalised anxiety disorder and panic disorder in adults (recommendations)
APA Practice Guideline for Panic Disorder, 2nd ed. (2009; legacy guideline)

offLabel.notes: Labeled for 'anxiety disorders' rather than panic disorder specifically. APA lists benzodiazepines as an option, but NICE advises against them for panic disorder because of poorer long-term outcomes. Same boxed warnings as other benzodiazepines (opioids; misuse; dependence and withdrawal).

details.labeledFor: Lorazepam and diazepam are FDA-approved for anxiety disorders; neither is specifically labeled for panic disorder.

dosing.start: Lorazepam 0.5 mg twice daily or diazepam 2 mg two to three times daily
dosing.target: Lorazepam 2–6 mg/day or diazepam 5–30 mg/day in divided doses
dosing.max: Lorazepam 10 mg/day; diazepam 40 mg/day (labeled anxiety maximums)
dosing.notes: Use short-term or as a bridge while an SSRI takes effect.

boxedWarnings: Concomitant use with opioids can cause profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death
warnings: Respiratory depression with opioids or alcohol
Dependence and withdrawal seizures if stopped abruptly
details.plainSummary: Benzodiazepines can calm panic quickly, but they are habit-forming and are usually kept to short-term use.

references.label: APA Practice Guideline for Panic Disorder, 2nd ed. (2009; legacy guideline)
NICE CG113: Generalised anxiety disorder and panic disorder in adults (recommendations)
